The starting point

Just this.

A random product photo I grabbed from Amazon: a neck fan. No model, no lifestyle photos, no script. Exactly the kind of input I'd expect day to day.

First move: clean it up. Drag the slider to see the original photo turn into a cutout that can go anywhere: listings, ads, video.

OriginalCutout

02
The model

A face for the concept.

I read the product as active, outdoor and fresh, so I generated a model and a world to match: a coastal run, soft morning light, colors pulled straight from the product.

Same character, every angle. That consistency is what lets one model carry a whole campaign. Tap the thumbnails.

Character consistencyArt directionPalette matching
03
The flyer

Benefits at a glance.

An explainer graphic built to work as an Amazon listing image or a social post: headline, four key benefits, and the moments it fits into a shopper's day.

Move your cursor over it, and tap the orange dots to see the thinking behind each decision.

Listing imagesCopyVisual hierarchy
1
Headline first: the benefit in two words, readable even as a thumbnail.
2
The model wears the product, so shoppers instantly understand how it's used.
3
Four benefits, four icons: scannable in under 3 seconds.
4
Use cases at the bottom widen the audience: gym, hiking, travel.
